name: @cloudgrid-io/mcp

tools.name: grid_pickup
tools.description: Pick up an app: copies any app the user can see into one of their grids as a NEW, separate entity (a fork, like a git fork). The copy records lineage back to the source and does not carry the source's secrets (the copy sets its own). Plugging the copy updates only the copy; the original is not changed. This is a fork, not a collab: it grants no access to the original entity, and it does not edit the original in place. Serves requests to copy, fork, remix, or make my own version of an app. Requires sign-in. Returns the copy's entity_id, slug, kind, grid, and lineage.

entity_id.description: The source app to copy: a canonical UUID or <grid-slug>/<entity-slug>.

grid.description: Grid to create your copy in. Required only when you belong to more than one grid.

name.description: Slug for your copy. Omit to derive one from the source.

source_version_id.description: Copy an older version instead of HEAD, e.g. v_a1b2c3d.

annotations.title: Copy an app into your grid

tools.name: grid_pull
tools.description: Pull an app to continue or edit it IN PLACE, like `git clone` of the SAME entity: the next plug with its target_entity_id updates that entity, and the team sees the new version. Requires push access (owner or collaborator). For an app the caller can only view, it returns can_edit: false and the options that remain (a separate copy, or push access to the same entity), and changes nothing. A drop plugged outside any grid is claimed into a chosen grid with its `claim_token`; only the drop's owner can claim it. Serves requests to continue, edit, or work on an app the user owns or collaborates on. Requires sign-in. Returns the entity_id, slug, grid, url, and whether the caller can edit it.

entity_id.description: The entity id to pull. Defaults to the drop made outside a grid in this session, if any.

grid.description: Grid to resolve a bare slug in. Required only when you belong to more than one grid.

claim_token.description: Claiming a drop plugged outside a grid: its owner token, which claims that drop into your grid. Only the drop's owner can claim it.

claim_url.description: Alternative to claim_token: the claim_url from the plug result; the token is read from it.

annotations.title: Pull an app to edit in place

tools.name: grid_collab
tools.description: Collab: grants the signed-in user PUSH ACCESS to the SAME live entity that someone else owns, as a collaborator on that entity, not a copy. It grants permission only and fetches nothing: no code is downloaded, no new entity is created, and no forked_from lineage is recorded. Plugs to the shared entity update it in place (the team sees the new version and can roll it back). When the owner gates who may join, it sends the owner an access request on the user's behalf, and access starts as soon as they approve. Serves requests to collab on, join, or get push or write access to an app the user does not own. Requires sign-in. Returns the entity_id, url, can_edit, and whether a request is pending.

entity_id.description: The app to get push access to: a canonical UUID or <grid-slug>/<entity-slug>.

grid.description: Grid to resolve a bare slug in. Required only when a bare slug is ambiguous across grids you belong to.

annotations.title: Get push access to an app you don't own

tools.name: grid_create_grid
tools.description: Create a new grid (the workspace the user's apps live in) for the signed-in user, who becomes its admin. Serves an account with no grid yet (a plug result of needs_grid_create, or a NO_ACTIVE_ORG failure) and requests to create a new grid or workspace. The slug is permanent and appears in app URLs. A new grid finishes setup in the background in about 30 seconds, and a plug into it waits for that setup. Requires sign-in. Returns the grid's slug and name, and whether setup is still running.

slug.description: The grid slug: 3-40 lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens, starting with a letter. Permanent: it appears in every app URL in the grid.

tools.name: grid_note
tools.description: Record a one-paragraph summary of what was built this session and why, for the local edition's optional QA session log, which the CloudGrid team reads. A successful plug posts the log on that same call, so a note sent after it is not recorded (the plug's session_note field carries a note on the plug itself). The log is dark unless the operator of this machine has set CLOUDGRID_QA_SLACK_WEBHOOK. Returns a short acknowledgement.

summary.description: A short plain-language summary of what was built and why.

tools.name: grid_plug
tools.description: Plug an app, website, game, or HTML page into CloudGrid at a live public URL. Serves requests to deploy, publish, host, ship, launch, go live, or share a working link: "give me a link", "share it with friends", "make it live", "put it online", "host this". Takes one source: `html` (a self-contained page) or `artifact_files` (a multi-file or database-backed runtime app; cloudgrid.yaml declares its needs), or `path` (local folder, file, or .zip). No target_entity_id (or grid+slug) creates a new URL; with one it updates it in place. Signed out it returns needs_auth and publishes nothing (the user signs in with the local browser sign-in); there is no guest publish. Also publishing nothing: needs_grid (several grids, listed), needs_grid_create (no grid yet), needs_confirmation (the source has a cloudgrid.yaml). Page source is public; known API key shapes are rejected. A runtime app returns status building while its build runs. Returns the URL and the entity_id (the re-plug handle).

html.description: A single self-contained HTML document to publish as an inspiration: the fast single-file path, live at a public URL in seconds. Pass the COMPLETE raw HTML inline (CSS+JS inline, images/fonts as data: URIs); a small fragment is wrapped into a full document. Raw text, not base64, and not an `@`-prefixed path or a file path. Mutually exclusive with `path` and `artifact_files`. Materialized as one index.html in the signed-in user's grid.

filename.description: Filename for the single-file `html` path. Defaults to index.html.

path.description: Local edition: path to the entity folder, a single file, or a .zip ARCHIVE to upload. A folder is read recursively, honoring .gitignore/.cloudgridignore (.git and node_modules are skipped). A .zip is extracted and plugged: with its own cloudgrid.yaml it plugs as that project; otherwise it becomes a static app (all files served). Serves "deploy this zip" / "gallery from these zipped images" requests. Mutually exclusive with `html` and `artifact_files`, EXCEPT `html` + a .zip of assets: the html becomes index.html over the archive's files (generate the page, let the zip supply the images).

artifact_files.description: The source inline, one entry per file, for hosted/no-filesystem transports (a multi-file app). A single HTML page fits `html`. On the local edition `path` reads the folder from disk. Sent INLINE (copied through this call), so large files (lockfiles, binaries) can truncate and fail the build; for a real framework, a lockfile, or binary assets, the disk-based CLI (`npx -y @cloudgrid-io/cli plug` where it is already signed in) is more reliable. Mutually exclusive with `html` and `path`.

path.description: Repo-relative path, e.g. index.html or services/web/index.js.

content.description: File content. Base64 when encoding is base64, otherwise UTF-8 text.

cloudgrid_yaml.description: Inline cloudgrid.yaml (the entity manifest). Optional; server auto-detection applies when omitted. On re-plug, a name: change is a warning only; the entity keeps its name and URL.

target_entity_id.description: Present → RE-PLUG: update this exact entity in place (same entity_id, slug, URL, plug history). Absent → CREATE a new entity. This is the durable handle a previous plug returned. Re-plugging a drop that was plugged outside a grid also needs its owner_token.

grid.description: On create: the grid slug to plug into, chosen by the user. Omitted for a user with more than one grid, the result is needs_grid with the grid list to choose from; a single-grid user is not asked. The grid sets the new entity's URL, which members can see it, and its datastore tier and namespace. On re-plug the entity stays in its grid grids, but pass its home grid here when it differs from your active grid (the API checks your membership in the entity's grid). A drop plugged outside a grid stays outside until its owner claims it into one.

slug.description: Alternative RE-PLUG handle: paired with `grid`, resolves to an existing entity (the pickup contract's replug_handle) and updates it in place, for a client that holds only grid+slug, not the raw entity_id. target_entity_id takes precedence. A grid+slug that does NOT resolve to an existing entity is treated as a CREATE (not a false-positive re-plug).

url.description: Alternative RE-PLUG handle: the entity's public CloudGrid URL (e.g. https://<grid>.cloudgrid.io/<slug>) for editing in place with the URL and no target_entity_id (the common "change the color of this page" flow). The grid is read from the host and the entity is resolved via the pickup contract, so no `grid` param is needed. target_entity_id and grid+slug take precedence. A non-CloudGrid host is ignored (it does not redirect the write); a URL that does not resolve is treated as a CREATE.

hints.description: Classification hints for the CREATE path (not entity targeting, which is target_entity_id).

kind.description: Force the detected kind; omit to let the server auto-detect.

yaml.description: An inline cloudgrid.yaml override used as a detection hint.

anon.description: Deprecated and ignored: it does not publish. A new plug needs sign-in: without it the result is needs_auth and nothing is published, even with anon: true. Editing a drop that was plugged outside a grid takes target_entity_id + owner_token.

owner_token.description: The owner token of a drop plugged outside a grid; it authorizes its re-plug (with target_entity_id). Re-minted on every such edit; the newest one from the result is the valid one.

confirm_new_app.description: Set true to confirm plugging a source that already contains a cloudgrid.yaml as a NEW runtime app. On a create, if the source has a cloudgrid.yaml and this is not set, the result is needs_confirmation and nothing is created (target_entity_id re-plugs an existing entity instead).

user_request.description: Local edition: a brief version of the user's request that led to this deploy, for the optional QA session log (dark unless this machine's operator set CLOUDGRID_QA_SLACK_WEBHOOK). Omit if the user asked not to share it.

session_note.description: Local edition: one short paragraph on what you built and why, for the optional QA session log.

annotations.title: Plug an app into the grid

tools.name: grid_get_app_source
tools.description: Retrieve the CURRENT deployed HTML of an inspiration/drop inline as text, for editing and re-plugging the SAME URL when its source is no longer in context (e.g. the user asks to 'change the color' of a page, even in a fresh chat with only its URL). Takes the entity_id from a plug result, the public url, or grid+slug; the session's last drop is the fallback. Given just a URL with no session, it resolves the entity_id via the pickup contract and also returns the entity's kind, single_html, capabilities (whether the caller may re-plug or fork it), and replug_handle. For a multi-file or runtime (app/agent) source it returns source_download_url, the route to the full source. Reads the HTML from the API server-side; read-only, creates nothing.

entity_id.description: The drop's durable id, from its plug result. Enough on its own: its URL is looked up. Falls back to this session's last drop.

url.description: The public URL of the drop (e.g. https://<grid>.cloudgrid.io/<slug>). Defaults to this session's last drop URL.

grid.description: Grid slug, used only to construct the URL when neither url nor session state is available.

slug.description: Entity slug, used with grid to construct the URL when neither url nor session state is available.

tools.name: grid_login
tools.description: Start a CLI-free CloudGrid sign-in. Serves requests to log in, sign in, or authenticate, and a plug result of needs_auth. Returns a URL to open in the browser, where the user completes the sign-in. Uses CloudGrid's existing OAuth.

tools.name: grid_login_status
tools.description: Finish a browser sign-in started from this server. Checks once: when the browser sign-in is complete, it saves the session and returns the signed-in email; otherwise it returns status pending.

code.description: The sign-in code. Defaults to the most recent sign-in started in this session.

tools.name: grid_visibility
tools.description: Change who can see a CloudGrid inspiration OR runtime app/agent. Simple modes: private (only the user), grid (everyone in their grid), link (anyone with the URL; indexed: true also makes it findable by search engines). Finer control via the TWO AXES instead: inside (who in the grid: private | spaces | grid) and outside (reach beyond it: none | link | public), with require_signin for a members-only link and `spaces` for selected spaces. 'authenticated' is retired (it maps to a sign-in-required link). Serves requests to make something private, restrict who sees it, or open it up. Takes the app's entity_id (from its plug result) or its url; the drop made earlier in the session is the fallback, and some hosts start a new session for every tool call. Kind-aware routing across both surfaces. Requires sign-in. Returns the stored visibility settings.

visibility.description: Simple mode: private | grid | link ('public' is an alias of link; indexed: true makes it search-findable; 'authenticated' is the retired alias for a sign-in-required link; 'space' needs the `spaces` list). Pass either this OR the inside/outside axes.

inside.description: Axis 1, who in the grid can see it: private (only the user), spaces (selected spaces, listed in `spaces`), or grid (everyone in the grid). Use together with `outside`, instead of `visibility`.

outside.description: Axis 2, reach beyond the grid: none, link (anyone with the link; add require_signin: true for signed-in accounts only), or public (anyone, and findable by search engines).

require_signin.description: With outside: link (or visibility: link): the link requires a signed-in CloudGrid account.

spaces.description: Space slugs, for inside: spaces (or the legacy space/grid modes).

indexed.description: With visibility: link, makes the page search-engine indexable.

entity_id.description: The app's entity_id, from its plug result. Falls back to this session's last drop.

url.description: The app's public URL, when the entity_id is not at hand. Resolved to its entity_id.

kind.description: Entity kind. Omit to auto-detect from this session's last drop (falls back to trying the runtime surface, then the inspiration surface).

grid.description: Grid of the entity. Defaults to the active grid.

tools.name: grid_check_deploy
tools.description: Check whether an async runtime-app build (a deploy, which here means a plug) has finished and the app is live. Serves a plug that returned status "building", and questions like "is it live yet?". Takes the entity_id from the plug result (or the app url), plus its poll_url when there is one; the session's last plug is the fallback, and some hosts start a new session for every tool call. Returns status (success, failed, building, queued, or unknown) and live, which is true only when the build succeeded and the URL serves; a failed build adds the reason, a log tail, and a suggested fix. Requires sign-in (builds are owned). Works on every edition, including hosted.

entity_id.description: The entity_id from the plug result. It finds the app's latest build. Falls back to this session's last plug.

url.description: The app's public URL, when the entity_id is not at hand (e.g. https://<slug>--<grid>.cloudgrid.io).

poll_url.description: The poll_url from a plug result, when it has one.

grid.description: Grid of the entity (the grid from the plug result). Defaults to the plug's grid, then the active grid.

tools.name: grid_list_grids
tools.description: List the signed-in user's grids, each with slug, name, role, whether it is the active grid, and setup status (render_ready). Requires sign-in. A plug into a brand-new grid waits for its setup by itself.

tools.name: grid_start
tools.description: A short orientation for building with CloudGrid: the account this session is signed in as and its active grid, how to choose between a single-page plug and a runtime app (and what each provides: managed database, Redis, pgvector, disk, an AI gateway with no API key), the sign-in and grid steps a first plug goes through, and the index of workflows that load by name. Read-only, under 3,000 characters. Serves a first look at CloudGrid and questions about what it can do or which account is connected. The full operating playbook is the doc named playbook.

tools.name: grid_get_template
tools.description: Load a specific CloudGrid workflow, template, example, rule, troubleshooting note, or reference doc by kind and name: deterministic retrieval from the bundled corpus, no network. Workflow and template names come from the orientation's workflow index, e.g. {kind:"workflow", name:"presentation"} or {kind:"template", name:"deck"}. Reference docs (kind "doc"): cloudgrid-yaml (the manifest schema and needs: vocabulary), capability-map (which template fits a request), playbook (the full operating rules). Returns the entry's full content.

tools.name: grid_report
tools.description: Report a genuine CloudGrid failure (a build, deploy, or platform call that failed unexpectedly) to the CloudGrid team, with the user's explicit consent. What is sent: the short `message` (what failed), the `context` passed (the tool, inputs, grid, original request, error code/detail), and the client name and platform: only the message and context the user agreed to send, nothing else from the conversation. Redaction is key-name-only: a value is dropped only when its KEY looks secret, so a secret embedded in a value (e.g. inside HTML) is sent as is. Returns the outcome status.

message.description: Short summary of what failed (required), not the whole conversation.

context.description: The failed-request context. Redaction is key-name-only (a value is dropped only when its KEY looks secret) client-side, and the server applies the same key-name filter; a secret embedded in a value is not redacted by either.

tool.description: The CloudGrid tool that failed, e.g. plug.

inputs.description: The failing inputs (e.g. the HTML/args), kept minimal. A secret embedded in a value here is not redacted.

grid.description: The grid/org slug involved, if any.

original_request.description: What the user asked for, in one line.

error_code.description: The server error code, e.g. INTERNAL_ERROR.

error_detail.description: The error message / detail surfaced to the agent.

category.description: Optional category, e.g. the failing tool name ("deploy"). Defaults to "mcp".

trace_id.description: The server's trace/deploy id from the failed response, if any (helps support pivot to the trace).

failed_step.description: The server-side pipeline step that failed, if known.

http_status.description: The HTTP status of the final failed request, if applicable.

tools.name: grid_hello
tools.description: Create a minimal hello page and plug it into the user's grid, returning the live URL. If the user has more than one grid and `grid` is not given, it returns needs_grid with the list and plugs nothing. Serves requests for a first test page or a quick check that plugging works. Requires sign-in.

grid.description: Grid slug to plug into. Omitted for a user with several grids, the result lists them.

tools.name: grid_create_project
tools.description: Scaffold a new CloudGrid app or agent folder (cloudgrid.yaml + a web service), optionally pre-declaring resources. Wraps `grid new` (scaffolds locally; no server entity exists until the folder is plugged). Language note: the nextjs starter is TypeScript (writes tsconfig.json + app/*.tsx), while CloudGrid templates are plain JavaScript. A template's files are the source of truth for the folder: its .js files replace the scaffolded tsconfig.json and app/*.tsx, so no route has both a .tsx and a .js file.

kind.description: Entity kind. 'agent' scaffolds an agent: block.

type.description: Seed a web service of this type.

needs.description: Pre-declare infrastructure needs in the scaffolded cloudgrid.yaml (e.g. ["database","ai"]).

dir.description: Target directory. Defaults to the current folder.

grid.description: Override the active grid this project will target.

cwd.description: Working directory. The CLI runs in this directory. Defaults to the MCP server's working directory.

tools.name: grid_view_logs
tools.description: Tail recent logs for an entity. Does not stream; returns a snapshot. Wraps `grid logs`.

name.description: Entity name. Omit to use the entity linked to the current directory.

since.description: Only logs newer than this, e.g. 5m, 1h, 2d.

tools.name: grid_share
tools.description: Set an entity's visibility and print its URL. Defaults to link (anyone with the URL). Wraps `grid visibility set`.

tools.name: grid_feedback
tools.description: List recent feedback events for the active grid. Read-only. Wraps `grid feedback list`.

since.description: Only events newer than this, e.g. 24h, 7d.

grid.description: Read another grid's feed where you have access.

tools.name: grid_whoami
tools.description: Show the signed-in user and active grid. Wraps `grid whoami`.

tools.name: grid_switch_grid
tools.description: Switch the active grid. Wraps `grid use`.

tools.name: grid_logout
tools.description: Sign out and clear local credentials. Wraps `grid logout`.

tools.name: grid_status
tools.description: Grid dashboard, entity detail, or deploy snapshot. Wraps `grid status`.

name.description: Entity name or trace id. Omit for the org dashboard.

tools.name: grid_info
tools.description: Show metadata for a CloudGrid entity. Wraps `grid info`.

name.description: Entity name. Omit for the entity linked to the current directory.

tools.name: grid_get
tools.description: List CloudGrid grids, entities, or spaces. Wraps `grid get <grids|entities|spaces> --json`.

resource.description: What to list: grids, entities, or spaces.

grid.description: Grid slug (entities/spaces only). Omit for the active grid.

space.description: Only entities scoped to this space slug (entities only).

tools.name: grid_describe_grid
tools.description: Show a grid's detail: role, members, spaces, tier, wildcard-TLS state. Wraps `grid describe grid <slug> --json`.

tools.name: grid_edit_existing_app
tools.description: Continue/edit an EXISTING entity locally: downloads its source + cloudgrid.yaml and links the folder so the next `grid plug` from it updates the entity IN PLACE. Requires push access (owner or collaborator). Wraps `grid pull`. It makes no copy and grants no access: a separate copy (a fork) and push access to an entity the user can only view (CLI: `grid collab <entity>`) are separate operations.

name.description: Entity slug or id to pull.

target_dir.description: Directory to pull into (relative to cwd). Defaults to the entity name.

grid.description: Grid to resolve the entity in. Defaults to the active grid.

version.description: Pull an older version's source instead of HEAD.

no_bind.description: Download source only, without cloudgrid.yaml and the link.

cwd.description: Working directory the CLI runs in. The download lands here; pass an explicit, writable directory.

tools.name: grid_rename
tools.description: Rename a CloudGrid entity's display name (slug stays the same). Wraps `grid rename`.

tools.name: grid_take_offline
tools.description: Take an entity off the grid. Destructive. Wraps `grid unplug`.

confirm.description: Set to true to confirm; the call is refused without it.

confirm.description: Set to true to confirm; the call is refused without it.

tools.description: Rollback an entity to a previous version. Wraps `grid rollback`.

to.description: Target version tag or id. Omit to roll back one version.

tools.name: grid_list_versions
tools.description: List published versions for an entity. Wraps `grid versions`.

name.description: Entity name. Omit for the entity linked to the current directory.

tools.name: grid_set_env
tools.description: Manage environment variables for an entity. Wraps `grid env`.

key.description: Variable name. Required for get and set.

cwd.description: Working directory. The CLI runs in this directory. Defaults to the MCP server's working directory.

tools.name: grid_set_secret
tools.description: Set or list secret names for an entity. Returns secret names only, not values. Wraps `grid secrets`.

cwd.description: Working directory. The CLI runs in this directory. Defaults to the MCP server's working directory.

tools.description: Scaffold service folders declared in cloudgrid.yaml (idempotent). Wraps `grid scaffold`.

cwd.description: Working directory. The CLI runs in this directory. Defaults to the MCP server's working directory.

tools.name: grid_diagnose
tools.description: Run CloudGrid diagnostics on the local environment. Wraps `grid doctor`.

tools.description: Return the public URL for an entity. Does not open a browser. Wraps `grid open --print`.

instructions:
CloudGrid runs the user's web apps at a live public URL and provides the infrastructure they need: managed MongoDB, Redis, pgvector, persistent disk, and an AI gateway that needs no API key. Every tool here is grid_*.

What it does, and the requests each tool serves:
- One self-contained HTML file becomes a live public URL in seconds: grid_plug with html (or path to the file). Serves "make it live", "put it online", "give me a link", "share it with friends", "plug it".
- A folder with several files, a framework, or anything that needs a database, a server, scheduled jobs, or an AI model, runs as a runtime app: grid_plug with path to the folder, with a cloudgrid.yaml that declares needs (needs: { database: true }, needs: { ai: true }); read the injected env vars lazily, inside handlers. Serves "deploy this app", "add a database", "let it call an AI model without my own key".
- Iterating keeps the same link: grid_plug with target_entity_id updates in place.
- Sharing and access: grid_visibility sets who can see it; grid_collab grants push access; grid_pickup copies any visible app's source.

What it does not do: it is not a shell, a container or VM host, or a Kubernetes target; it does not deploy a git repository from a URL; it does not run desktop or mobile apps.

How a plug works: creating anything needs a signed-in account (a signed-out create returns needs_auth; call grid_login, then grid_login_status after the browser step, then plug again). No grid yet: grid_plug returns needs_grid_create; suggest a slug, confirm it with the user, call grid_create_grid, then plug with that grid right away. More than one grid: it returns needs_grid; ask which. Never write an API key into page source or app code — needs: { ai: true } gives the app the managed AI gateway with no key, and other keys go in grid secrets (grid_plug rejects known key shapes). A runtime build is asynchronous: poll grid_check_deploy with its entity_id about every 15 seconds until success before saying it is live. End with the live URL.

Editing and access: to edit a page whose HTML is not in context, call grid_get_app_source first, then grid_plug with target_entity_id. "Collab" or "join" on someone else's app is grid_collab, not grid_pickup; it grants push access only, then grid_pull or grid_edit_existing_app gets the code. If a pull reports view-only, say so and offer grid_pickup (a separate copy) or grid_collab. Confirm with the user before grid_delete or grid_take_offline. Send grid_report only after the user agrees. grid_note feeds the optional QA log: send it before a plug, or pass grid_plug's session_note.

For shell steps, run the CLI as `npx -y @cloudgrid-io/cli@latest <command>` (never a bare `grid`); `grid dev` runs the app locally with the same services. grid_start returns a short orientation and the workflow index; grid_get_template loads workflows, templates, and reference docs.
